checks.claim: C1: Exact original objects and coupling
checks.reason: Contract lines 13-18 keep the full d1 class: 0<a<1, 0<alpha<=1, alpha+a<2, Gamma a nonzero homogeneous nonnegative Radon covariance, and the raw kernel |t-s|^-a. There is no fBm normalization, projection or discard. This matches direct-event lines 83-91 and phase-response lines 9-11. Z=W(psi) uses the same common W (line 17). Line 18 explicitly declines the premise that each cutoff is measurable from the raw field, consistent with interaction-driver lines 216-231. I checked the distributional Jacobian independently: substituting t=delta u gives W^delta(f)=delta^(a/2-1)W(f(./delta,.)), whose covariance equals the raw covariance, so W^delta has the raw law. In fast time the semiclassical equation delta^2 V_tt=V_xx+sqrt(delta)WV becomes V_uu=V_xx+delta^((1-a)/2)W^delta V, which confirms g. This matches local-flow (7.1) and interaction-driver (B0). The masked HS coordinates are the source construction W_R(f)=W(zeta_R f) (local-flow lines 114-117), applied with T=L and R=r.

checks.claim: C2: Phi in (A) is an everywhere-defined continuous linear map on the full B into operator-driver paths on F, and Phi(X)=A
checks.reason: For any x in B, x_j(u) is in HS(E), which is contained in B(E), and K:F->E is bounded. Here kappa is compact smooth, and the proof of local-flow (4.2), a finite rho_l chi_l expansion, applies to any such kappa. Multiplication by rho_j is bounded on E and gives compactly supported E phases. These embed continuously in F (local-flow lines 173-176). I is finite. So Phi(x)(u) is in B(F), Phi(x)(0)=0, and the Holder increments are bounded by C(||K||, max_j||rho_j||) times sum_j[x_j]_theta, with no compatibility needed. The agreement Phi(X)=A follows exactly from the local-flow construction: the output of M_R and its input-vanishing support lie in [-2R-T,2R+T]=O for R=r, T=L (lines 144-151). A is defined on F via the global-E operator applied to kappa v (lines 212-216). chi_j=1 on supp rho_j (lines 161-162). Sum over I of rho_j equals 1 on O because the omitted rho_j vanish on O. The mask is never commuted with S. e0=(1,0) is in F, and K e0=(kappa,0) is compact smooth. This is a sound, non-vacuous fixed-parameter target. The constant C_(r,L) carries a sum over roughly r+L indices, which is correctly flagged as not replacing the MAX bound (4.4).

checks.claim: C3: Covariance shift, exact cancellation (C), rescaling, shifted potential and block phase
checks.reason: Bochner integrability: X lies in L^2(B), so E||XZ||_B <= ||X||_(L2 B) v^(1/2). Phi is bounded linear, so Phi(b)=E[Phi(X)Z]=E[AZ], taken on the separable closed range. I computed independently: E[W^delta(f)Z]=delta^(a/2-1)E[W(f(./delta))W(psi)]=delta^(a/2) times the integral of f(u,x)h(delta u,x), with h exactly as in line 86. Hence E[A(u)Z]=g delta^(a/2) H_delta(u)=sqrt(delta)H_delta(u), using g delta^(a/2)=delta^(1/2). This confirms (C) and the amplitude identity in line 138. H_delta is a strong integral, as in local-flow (5.5), and is Lipschitz into B(F). No norm continuity of S is used. In the masking, the mask radius r=c/delta is kept distinct from the physical R=T delta (lines 22-23). The fast-block slow time m delta+delta u and the phase (V,partial_u V)=(V,delta partial_t V) are correct, with the fractional block retained.

checks.claim: C4a: Tilt (T), sign, half-cost, degenerate covariance, Borel generation and version safety
checks.reason: Under e^(lambda Z - lambda^2 v/2)dP, the law of X is the law of X+lambda b. With lambda=-1/sqrt(delta) and test x -> j(x+b/sqrt(delta)), this gives E j(X), so the sign and v/(2delta) are correct. Evaluation at rational q composed with HS matrix coordinates in a Schwartz ONB gives countably many continuous linear functionals that separate points of B: HS matrices determine the operator, and paths are continuous. B is Polish, so these generate the Borel sigma-algebra, and finite cylinders form a pi-system. Joint Gaussianity of these coordinates with Z therefore determines both laws without inverting any covariance. The cases v=0 and singular covariance are trivial or covered. The density is positive with mean 1, so the measures are equivalent. Because j is defined on all of B, changing versions of X only changes null sets.

checks.claim: C4b: J_delta is a continuous nonnegative function on B, and the post-tilt observable is the actual retained-potential local Young flow
checks.reason: J_delta is a composition of continuous maps: Phi (continuous linear), the locally Lipschitz Young map (5.3), the bounded S(L) on F, and the bounded compact-test functional on F (via (4.2)). It is therefore continuous and nonnegative. By (A) and (C), J_delta(X+b/sqrt(delta)) uses the driver A+H_delta, the interaction primitive for g zeta_r W^delta + zeta_r h(delta u). The compactly supported W^(1,inf) profile is admissible (local-flow lines 303-327). No nonzero-profile canonical series, independent increments or raw point evaluation is assumed (lines 110-111, 139-141). I found no circular premise.

checks.claim: C4c: Noise-only canonical average, and the average-to-original-point moment map with its exact pinpoint support
checks.reason: The mathematics holds. The cone condition is M+L <= c/delta, which holds when c >= 1+M delta, and so whenever c >= 1+M (needed for local-flow (6.1)). The scaling identity is direct-event Section 1. The inequality E|int phi u(T,R.)|^2 <= E u(T,0)^2 is valid for nonnegative unit-mass phi. The statement's support is defective, however. Contract lines 114-115 cite 'the accepted phase-response Section6 average inequality'. Phase-response Section 6 (lines 348-378) is endpoint/scope calibration and contains no such inequality. The inequality is phase-response (M), Section 5, lines 302-325. Also, contract lines 6-9 declare that the accepted analytic inputs are 'exactly' interaction-driver Sections 5-6, local-flow Sections 3-7 and direct-event Section 1. phase-response is not on that list, yet the statement uses it directly as the load-bearing consumer toward the original POINT target. The input boundary and the pinpoint are internally inconsistent.

checks.claim: C5: Profile admissibility, non-vacuity and retained scope
checks.reason: psi is in C_c^infinity((0,1)xR), extended by zero to a smooth function. So G(s)=Gamma*psi(s) and its s-derivatives are C_b^1, using c|x|^-alpha, 0<alpha<1, with derivatives moved onto psi, or c delta for white noise. Then h(t)=int|tau|^-a G(t-tau)dtau over |tau|<=2 is bounded and Lipschitz (indeed C^1) into C_b^1 on [0,1]. The decay of Gamma*psi gives spatial C^1 tails tending to 0 uniformly in t, so (5.6) holds with c(t)=0. zeta_r h is supported in [-2r,2r] with uniform W^(1,inf) bounds for r>=1, and r=c/delta>=1. In d1 the even homogeneous class is exactly Riesz or white (phase-response lines 178-181), and a nonzero test has positive variance. The open items (spectral complement/product/event, optimizer map, source constant, normalization, profile-shifted mask independence, higher dimensions and sharp constants) are retained at lines 159-166. Lines 147-149 make no moment-rate or source theorem claim.

limitations: This is a statement-fidelity review, not a proof audit. The prior notes were treated as scoped accepted inputs and were not re-proved.
The Jacobian, the covariance cancellation (C), the tilt sign and half-cost, the cone radius, Borel generation and profile admissibility were checked by hand. No Lean or numerical checks were run.
Classifying the citation and input-boundary defect as blocking is a judgment. The statement is otherwise sound and worth proving, and after the single citation repair I would expect C4c to pass.

Confidence is medium overall: high on the C1-C3 and C5 checks and on the factual existence of the defect, but the blocking classification is a judgment call. This does not meet the HIGH acceptance threshold.
Not a novelty, whole-paper or source-text audit; no external sources were consulted.
